caption: The drawing depicts a clear glass oil lamp positioned centrally on a plain, off-white background. The lamp has a round, transparent glass reservoir that reveals the wick inside, which is a light tan color. The body of the lamp sits atop an ornate, fluted stem that rests on a broad, scalloped base, all rendered in shades of transparent and reflective gray to suggest the glass material. At the top, the lamp has a brass burner with a round knob for adjusting the wick; the burner is colored in golds and browns with small perforations and two curved metal supports. The drawing is made with colored pencils or watercolors, evidencing careful shading and attention to the glass's reflective and refractive qualities. At the bottom right corner, the name “Carl Buergerriss” is written in small, neat script. There are no other objects or elements in the composition.
title: Glass Oil Lamp
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
